why: A signed record is permanent; the SUBJECT it describes is not. When a Note is converted to a Page, unpublished, or otherwise leaves the posts corpus, its anchored record stays exactly where it is — but two coverage checks then contradict each other: verify-coverage's reverse check demands every record directory have an index row, while its forward check demands every index row have a live post. No converted subject can satisfy both. This file is the third answer: the retirement is STATED, with a date and a reason, so the exemption is evidence rather than silence. Records are never edited or removed to satisfy a check.

retired.reason: Converted from a Note to a Page, so it no longer answers on /wp/v2/posts. The v2 record remains anchored (genesis leaf, bitcoin block 957359) and untouched; only its index row stops being emitted, because build-index derives entries from the live posts endpoint.
